question: The position vector of a point $P$ is the sum of the vectors $2\hat{i}-3\hat{j}+4\hat{k}$ and $-5\hat{i}+\hat{j}+2\hat{k}$. Find the coordinates of $P$ and verify its position vector.
explanation:
Step 1: Addition of the given vectors
The position vector of $P$ is
\(\overrightarrow{OP}=(2\hat{i}-3\hat{j}+4\hat{k})+(-5\hat{i}+\hat{j}+2\hat{k})\)
Step 2: Combination of corresponding components
\(\overrightarrow{OP}=(2-5)\hat{i}+(-3+1)\hat{j}+(4+2)\hat{k}\)
Therefore,
\(\overrightarrow{OP}=-3\hat{i}-2\hat{j}+6\hat{k}\)
Step 3: Identification of coordinates
The coefficients of $\hat{i}$, $\hat{j}$ and $\hat{k}$ give the coordinates of $P$. Hence, $P=(-3,-2,6)$.
Step 4: Verification
The position vector of $(-3,-2,6)$ is $-3\hat{i}-2\hat{j}+6\hat{k}$, which agrees with the calculated vector.
Final Answer
$P=(-3,-2,6)$.
